title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and opened the floor to public comment before moving on to their official agenda.

After Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order, she called on Lori Sturm who asked to address the council about a fundraiser.  Sturm said the fundraiser is to raise money for her Brother-In-Law Ted Young.  They are hoping to use the REA Building and rain shelter at Charley Brown Park on Saturday, June 13.  They would like to host a 3k or 5k run, a fishing derby and an auction and silent auction.  Commissioners asked questions and the consensus was that a race would create issues.  The fishing derby and auctions at the park were approved with appropriate insurance documentation.  Next, Flora High School is asking that the streets around New Beginnings Church on West North Avenue be closed for Promenade on Saturday, April 25 and commissioners approved their request.  Also, JoAnna Spicer with the Illinois Breast and Cervical Cancer Program asked to use the rain Shelter at Charley Brown Park for an event on Saturday, May 30 and after a couple of brief comments, commissioners approved her request.

The official meeting then got underway, and the council quickly approved the meeting agenda and consent agenda.  The latter included approval of the past meeting minutes and warrant list; the event schedule of the Flora Coon Club, including the Bluetick Breeders and Coonhunters Association Spring Round-Up April 15-18 and Black and Tan Days April 29-May 2; the recycling event on May 16 from 9:00-11:00am at the city owned parking lot in downtown Flora near the police station; and approval of the community farmer’s market on Saturday 8:00am-Noon at Library Park from May 23-October 24.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer proclaimed April 12-18 as Public Safety Telecommunicators Week and honored the people who work at the 911 Call Center in Flora, including Jennifer Brown, Michael Dickerson, Nancy Dehart, Billy Laughlin and Jennifer Wainscott.  These Telecommunicators ask for people to remember that if you accidentally call 911, don’t hang up.  Stay on the line with then and explain what happened.  You are not in any trouble.  If you hang up, the 911 dispatcher will be calling you back in order to verify if there is an emergency or not.  If you are having a controlled burn, please call in on the non-emergency line to let the 911 dispatcher know so they don’t send out the fire department to put out your fire.  Another request from 911 is to please do not let your child play with your phone as it is so easy for them to accidentally dial 911, when they hear a voice, they hang up.  Parents, don’t get mad at the child for calling 911.  Explain to them the do’s and don’ts of 911.  For non-emergent calls in Flora call (618) 662-9111 and for others in Clay County, call (618) 665-3316.

In other regular business, Mayor Spicer asked commissioners to accept the resignation of Brad Thompson from the Ethics Commission, effective March 15, which they quickly did.  Members approved Dawn Wiles to the Tourism Committee, with Commissioner Phil Wiley noting that they need another member of the Tourism Committee and he asked for suggestions for who might serve.  They also appointed Bill Seelman to the Ethics Commission.  Both Wiles and Seelman’s appointments began April 6 for two year terms.

The mayor then polled commissioners for their comments.  Jeremy Henderson asked the council to approve the Flora Swimming Pool Schedule and Fees and employees for the 2025 season, which they did.  Logan Atwood will be the Pool Manager and Callie Johnson Assistant Manager.  The pool at Charley Brown Park opens on Saturday, May 23 and closes Sunday, August 9.  Daily hours are 12:00-5:00pm with adult swim time from 5:00-6:00pm.  Admission is $5 with Military and First Responders Free with their ID.  Seniors age 55 and up $3 and age three and under are free.  An individual pass is $125, family pass is $200 for up to 4 members and $25 for each additional member.  Pool parties are $250 and private sponsorship is $450 during the day and $350 for night events.

Commissioner Phil Wiley used his time to note that some people have commented on higher utility bills due to natural gas prices.  He noted that the city does offer budget billing to help customers even out costs in an affordable manner.  Contact city hall about signing up for budget billing.  He said the program is also available for people who rent their homes, but they will need to get approval from their landlord.  He also called attention to the fact that people can sign up for email delivery of their utility bill and go paperless and eliminate delays with postal delivery.  He also reminds people with charitable intentions that they can help their fellow neighbors with high utility costs to make a donation through the City of Flora to the Clay County Ministerial Alliance.

As the meeting continued, Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger said there is an effort in Jefferson County to form a Major Case Squad for Southern Illinois and he asked the Flora City Council to approve the Downstate Major Case Squad Intergovernmental Criminal Justice Service Agreement, and they unanimously approved it.  Commissioners also approved  Chief Ruger’s request to approve the change of ownership of the K-9 Hektor to the K-9 Duke, with thanks for Hektor’s service to the city.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford called on Lee Beckman with Milano and Grunloh Engineers of Effingham for a brief update on the status of Flora’s grant application progress.  Among the topics Beckman addressed was the Safe Routes to School Sidewalk Construction Grants.  He stated construction could begin in May for the first round of that grant.  Stanford then asked commissioners to approve the revised City of Flora Employee Handbook, noting several updates to the handbook dealing with residency, payroll, vacations, holidays, sick days, etc.  It was approved without dissent.  They also approved Stanford’s request to approve an ordinance seeking bids on the property at 121 W. Maple.  Bids are accepted until 10:00am on April 16.  Stanford also commented on the proposed wastewater treatment plant.  He said he’d heard from Matt Johnson and he told Stanford that Flora’s proposal is still within the EPA guidelines, adding that projects that are not compliant are facing a 25% increase in costs.

Before adjourning, City Clerk Kaci O’Dell earned approval of the resolution concerning the release of closed session minutes.  And Treasurer Stephanie Bailey noted that commissioners have the proposed budget for the new fiscal year and it is available for public inspection.  Prior to its approval at the next meeting, a public hearing will be held in advance of that meeting.  Just before the meeting closed, Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles noted that construction continues on the bathrooms at the pickleball courts.

title: CASH IN TOP 10
full_story:
Haven Cash, FFA Section 23 President, from North Clay High School, has been named one of the top Section Presidents in the state.

Ten students were recently named Illinois FFA Top 10 Section Presidents in recognition of excelling in their role as an Illinois FFA Section President.  They will be recognized for their achievement later this year during the 2026 Illinois FFA State Convention.

Across Illinois, 25 FFA Section presidents lead the schools and students in their section while serving on the state officer team, which is led by the six Illinois FFA Major State Officers.

As a Top Section President, students are invited to attend the Premier 20 Leadership Conference held April 27th through 28th in Bloomington.  The conference is an opportunity for youth in agriculture from FFA and 4-H to further cultivate leadership and professional development skills.

Illinois Farm Bureau and Affiliates Youth Education in Agriculture Committee seek to cultivate the next generation of leaders in Illinois and are the proud sponsors of both the Illinois FFA Top 10 Section President award and Premier 20 Leadership conference.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
With a Blood Emergency in place throughout the Midwest, the American Red Cross is asking area blood donors to get out and give blood at their next earliest opportunity.

In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have a blood drive on Tuesday, April 14th at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church from Noon to 6 pm.  Then there will be a blood drive on Thursday, April 16th from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

Those who give blood or platelets at these drives will get a $15 e-gift card to the merchant of their choice.

After next weeks drives the next Blood drives in our area will be on Tuesday, April 21st at the Floyd Henson JR High and then on Tuesday, April 28th at the Flora High School.

title: I57 LANE CLOSURE
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced the closure of one of the southbound lanes of I-57 at mile marker 132 three miles south of Farina through 4:30 Friday afternoon.

The lane closure will allow for AIDOT District 8 Operations forces to perform emergency bridge deck repairs on the bridge over the East Fork of the Kaskaskia River.

IDOT says motorists can expect delays and should allow extra time for trips through the area.  Drivers are urged to pay close attention to changed conditions and signs in the work zones, obey the posted speed limits, refrain from using mobile devices, and be alert for workers and equipment.

title: DISTRACTED DRIVING AWARENESS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation is partnering with the Illinois State Police and local law enforcement agencies across the state during April, reminding the public to put their phones away and pay attention to the road.  Throughout the month, additional law enforcement officers will be watching for texting, social media use, video viewing and other forms of distracted driving.

“Too many drivers think they can glance at a text, check a notification or scroll for a second and still drive safely,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, IDOT’s bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering.  “They cannot.  Distracted driving takes eyes off the road, hands off the wheel and attention away from what matters most.”

According to IDOT statistics, 253 people died and 28,271 people were injured in crashes involving distractions between 2020 and 2024 in Illinois.  In 2024, 51 people were killed in crashes involving at least one distracted driver, accounting for 4.3% of all traffic fatalities that year.

Illinois law prohibits drivers from manually using an electronic communication device while operating a motor vehicle, including to text, stream video, participate in video conferences or access social media.  Even legal hands-free use can still take a driver’s attention off the road.

“We’ve all seen it while driving.  The person in the car next to you or in front of you who keeps looking down at their phone, starts to drift into the next lane, only to jerk back at the last minute,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Chris Owen.  “Every day, ISP handles avoidable crashes caused by someone driving while distracted, many times because they were texting.  No text is more important than your life.  Don’t drive distracted.”

The traffic safety effort is a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration campaign focused on distracted-driving prevention.  The heightened enforcement in Illinois is made possible through federal funds administered by IDOT and coincides with its comprehensive multimedia campaign “It’s Not a Game.”
